request.system:
You explain a fitted credit-risk model to a credit risk manager who is not a data scientist. You receive the facts about one model and write a short explanation of what drives its predictions of default.

# The text

- Write 5 to 8 sentences in plain English, most important drivers first.
- Mention an interaction when it matters for the model's predictions.
- Say only what the facts support. Do not round a weak effect up to a strong one, and do not add knowledge about credit risk that the facts do not show.
- When the facts do not settle something, say so ("the data do not settle whether ...") or leave it out.

# The answer

Return one JSON object with one list, `sentences`, each with an `id` (1, 2, 3, ...) and its `text`.
messages:
These are the facts about the model.

Model: an explainable boosting machine (EBM), fitted to predict whether a credit applicant defaults (5,000 applicants). Effects are on the log-odds scale: positive values raise the risk of default. Every band is a 95% band from 100 refits of the model on resampled data.

Features, in the order of their share of the model's importance:
- `utilization`: revolving credit utilization: the share of the credit limit in use (0 to 1).
  Share of importance 39.0% (95% band 30.3% to 43.1%); rank 1 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): x < 0.441: -0.5; 0.441 <= x < 0.626: +0.3; 0.626 <= x < 0.746: +1.4; x >= 0.746: +3.1 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +3.09, 95% band [+2.54, +3.68]).
- `n_delinquencies`: number of past delinquencies on the credit file (0 to 6).
  Share of importance 19.3% (95% band 12.0% to 20.3%); rank 2 to 3 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): 0: -0.3; >= 1: +0.3 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.86, 95% band [+0.56, +1.01]).
- `income`: annual income in US dollars.
  Share of importance 10.8% (95% band 7.7% to 14.1%); rank 2 to 4 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): x < 47,300: +0.2; x >= 47,300: 0 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.63, 95% band [-0.94, -0.25]).
- `history_months`: length of the credit history in months.
  Share of importance 7.0% (95% band 3.8% to 10.9%); rank 3 to 7 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): falls by 0.52 (95% band [-0.80, -0.25]) from x = 23.5 (5th percentile) to x = 341 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `age`: age of the applicant in years.
  Share of importance 6.9% (95% band 2.7% to 10.1%); rank 4 to 8 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): falls by 0.30 (95% band [-0.59, -0.01]) from x = 23.7 (5th percentile) to x = 72.3 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `dti`: debt-to-income ratio (0 to 0.6).
  Share of importance 5.9% (95% band 2.1% to 9.1%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): rises by 0.28 (95% band [+0.03, +0.52]) from x = 0.0291 (5th percentile) to x = 0.568 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `n_inquiries`: number of recent credit inquiries.
  Share of importance 3.4% (95% band 0.3% to 7.8%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): rises by 0.20 (95% band [+0.00, +0.51]) from x = 0 (5th percentile) to x = 4 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `months_at_address`: months at the current address (standardised).
  Share of importance 2.2% (95% band 0.9% to 5.4%); rank 5 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.14, 95% band [-0.49, +0.09]).
- `num_dependents`: number of dependents (standardised).
  Share of importance 1.0% (95% band 0.4% to 5.2%); rank 6 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.03, 95% band [-0.28, +0.20]).

Interactions: the model has 5 pairs. The larger ones:
- `history_months & n_inquiries`: share of importance 1.7% (95% band 0.0% to 3.3%).
  Effect of `history_months` from 23.5 to 341: -0.39 (95% band -0.66 to -0.02) when `n_inquiries` = 0, -0.78 (95% band -1.29 to -0.27) when `n_inquiries` = 4.
  Effect of `n_inquiries` from 0 to 4: +0.38 (95% band +0.00 to +0.74) when `history_months` = 23.5, -0.02 (95% band -0.42 to +0.51) when `history_months` = 341.
- `n_delinquencies & months_at_address`: share of importance 0.8% (95% band 0.0% to 2.2%).
  Effect of `n_delinquencies` from 0 to 2: +0.77 (95% band +0.49 to +1.00) when `months_at_address` = -1.66, +0.87 (95% band +0.55 to +1.01) when `months_at_address` = 1.64.
  Effect of `months_at_address` from -1.66 to 1.64: -0.18 (95% band -0.51 to +0.09) when `n_delinquencies` = 0, -0.07 (95% band -0.48 to +0.11) when `n_delinquencies` = 2.
- `utilization & n_inquiries`: share of importance 0.8% (95% band 0.0% to 1.8%).
  Effect of `utilization` from 0.0904 to 0.744: +3.17 (95% band +2.56 to +3.82) when `n_inquiries` = 0, +3.02 (95% band +2.53 to +3.64) when `n_inquiries` = 4.
  Effect of `n_inquiries` from 0 to 4: +0.27 (95% band +0.00 to +0.63) when `utilization` = 0.0904, +0.12 (95% band -0.05 to +0.44) when `utilization` = 0.744.
- `dti & age`: share of importance 0.7% (95% band 0.0% to 3.0%).
  Effect of `dti` from 0.0291 to 0.568: +0.27 (95% band -0.00 to +0.52) when `age` = 23.7, +0.20 (95% band -0.15 to +0.52) when `age` = 72.3.
  Effect of `age` from 23.7 to 72.3: -0.25 (95% band -0.55 to +0.15) when `dti` = 0.0291, -0.32 (95% band -0.66 to -0.00) when `dti` = 0.568.
- `utilization & dti`: share of importance 0.6% (95% band 0.0% to 2.5%).
  Effect of `utilization` from 0.0904 to 0.744: +3.03 (95% band +2.53 to +3.68) when `dti` = 0.0291, +3.14 (95% band +2.54 to +3.84) when `dti` = 0.568.
  Effect of `dti` from 0.0291 to 0.568: +0.16 (95% band -0.36 to +0.51) when `utilization` = 0.0904, +0.27 (95% band +0.03 to +0.54) when `utilization` = 0.744.

Write the explanation.

content.text: {"sentences":[{"id":1,"text":"The model's predictions of default are driven mainly by how much of their credit limit an applicant is using: utilization accounts for about 39% of the model's importance, and its band is roughly 30% to 43%."},{"id":2,"text":"Risk rises sharply at high utilization: below about 44% the effect is a small reduction in risk, while above about 75% it adds roughly 3.1 units to the log-odds of default, the largest single effect in the model."},{"id":3,"text":"The number of past delinquencies is the second driver, at about 19% of importance (band roughly 12% to 20%): an applicant with no delinquencies gets a small reduction in risk, and any delinquency adds a moderate increase."},{"id":4,"text":"Income matters less, at about 11% of importance, with a clear pattern only at the threshold of about 47,300 dollars: incomes below that add a small amount of risk, and higher incomes add none."},{"id":5,"text":"Credit history length, applicant age, debt-to-income ratio and recent inquiries each carry only small shares of importance (roughly 2% to 7%), and their effects are modest and uncertain, with bands that often touch zero."},{"id":6,"text":"Months at address and number of dependents show no effect that the data can distinguish from zero, so they should not be read as drivers of default in this model."},{"id":7,"text":"The main interaction is between history length and recent inquiries, but it is small (about 2% of importance, band 0% to 3%), so the data do not firmly settle how these two features combine."},{"id":8,"text":"The other interactions, including those involving utilization with inquiries or debt-to-income, are also small and have bands that include zero, so the utilization effect can be read as roughly the same across the other features' values."}]}
